question_text: The Commission on Audit (COA) has been given a budget allocation by Congress that is significantly lower than what it requested. The COA Chairperson argues that this violates the constitutional provision on fiscal autonomy. Under Article IX of the 1987 Constitution, which of the following best describes the fiscal autonomy granted to constitutional commissions like the COA?

options.text: Constitutional commissions have the right to determine their own budgets without interference from Congress.
Constitutional commissions are entitled to an automatic appropriation of funds equal to their previous year's budget adjusted for inflation.
Constitutional commissions enjoy fiscal autonomy, meaning they cannot be subjected to budgetary cuts that impair their independence, but Congress still has the power to appropriate funds.
Constitutional commissions have no fiscal autonomy; they are entirely dependent on the annual appropriations from Congress.
